review_comment: What does `bazel build //:all` report in this context? Does it automatically fold the alias and actual into the same output report or does it keep them as separate entries?

before:

```
% bazelisk build :cli :alias  --use_top_level_targets_for_symlinks --show_result=2
Starting local Bazel server and connecting to it...
INFO: Analyzed 2 targets (59 packages loaded, 976 targets configured).
INFO: Found 2 targets...
WARNING: cleared convenience symlink(s) bazel-bin, bazel-testlogs because their destinations would be ambiguous
Target //:cli up-to-date:
  bazel-out/applebin_macos-darwin_arm64-fastbuild-ST-9e7e65650639/bin/cli
Target //:cli up-to-date:
  bazel-out/applebin_macos-darwin_arm64-fastbuild-ST-9e7e65650639/bin/cli
INFO: Elapsed time: 7.179s, Critical Path: 0.39s
INFO: 8 processes: 4 internal, 3 darwin-sandbox, 1 local.
INFO: Build completed successfully, 8 total actions
```

after:

```
% bazel-dev build :cli :alias  --use_top_level_targets_for_symlinks --show_result=2
INFO: Analyzed 2 targets (0 packages loaded, 0 targets configured).
INFO: Found 2 targets...
Target //:cli up-to-date:
  bazel-bin/cli
Target //:cli up-to-date:
  bazel-bin/cli
INFO: Elapsed time: 0.083s, Critical Path: 0.00s
INFO: 1 process: 1 internal.
INFO: Build completed successfully, 1 total action
```
(all vs specifying multiple targets is the same)
So this is an improvement for this, as previously the alias vs target were different configurations it seems

Interesting. The reporting is still a big confusing since it doesn't acknowledge why `//:cli` is reported twice. But that's orthogonal to what you're doing - just an observation.

Thanks for the explanation. I don't see any scenario where the alias's direct configuration is relevant for this.
